page.layout: Two printed pages on one scan: the left page is only a fragment of margin text (left-edge notes, all of it marginal); the right page has one text block of running italic text in a single column, with a running head "LIBER I." and page number 531 at the top, a signature "Ll 2" at the foot, and no notes in its own margin.

p.i: Vidimus Monarchiam & statum politicum perfectum, tam respectu finis absoluti; quam respectu finis eminentis: restant aliquot distinctiones Monarchiæ. Est enim Monarchia alia perfectior, alia minus perfecta.

Monarchia perfectior est, in qua princeps, siue Monarcha nullius simpliciter dominium agnoscit, praterquam solius Dei, simulq; instructus ea est aplitudine ditionis, nepe oppidorum, pagorum, urbium & prouinciarum, & ea quoque opum ac virium potentia, ut subditos suos non tantum recte, sed etiam ornatè ac splendidè gubernare possit.
Imperfectior monarchia est vel ratione potestatis, vel ratione territorii, vel ratione utriusque simul.
Imperfectior Monarchia ratione potestatis iterum est vel ratione alicuius superioris, vel ratione specialium pactorum, vel ratione mixtionis, vel denique ratione temporis.
Imperfecta Monarchia ratione potestatis superioris, iterum est vel ratione potestatis superioris proprie dicta, vel improprie dicta.
Superior proprie dictus est, cuius potestatem inferior agnoscit, ita ut obædientiam ei debeat.

main_text.p: Sic Principes Germaniæ sunt Monarchæ, nepe suorum Principatuum respectu, agnoscunt enim superiorem, nempe ipsum Imperatorem, tanquam superiorem & perfectiorem Monarcham.

page.notes: The left page is a fragment of the neighbouring page's text and margin notes (cut-off words such as "inter", "Christ", "diuin", "exitus"); it is not transcribed further. Italic type is used for the body text of the right page; the long s is printed as s throughout. Some words in the right column are partly obscured by the binding and may be misread.
